turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): doctor, mr keane is in. pressure just now was one fifty two over ninety, ah no, one fifty eight over ninety four. pulse seventy eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): thanks. what's brought you in?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): it's the ankles, doctor, they're swelled up, and i'm passing urine the whole time. i can't get the good shoes on after the tea, and in tesco i have to know where the jacks is, it's mortifying. the wife has been at me for weeks but sure the garden was in bits.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): how long is the swelling there?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): a fortnight... no, i'm wrong, it's six weeks. i was mixing it up with the week the dog was sick, god love him. six weeks, both ankles, worse of an evening.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): pain in them?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): no pain. just the swelling, and if you press the left one the dent stays, i showed the chemist and he poked at it and said it was the tablet.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): passing urine how often?

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): umm nearly every hour through the day, and twice in the night, twenty past two and half five, i looked at the clock. the stream is grand, no burning, and i do drink a fierce amount of tea, always have, breakfast till bedtime.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): any fever?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): no. no fever. not once, and i'd know, i'm a cold creature normally.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): cough?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): no. no cough.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): weight up or down?

[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): ah i couldn't tell you. the scales are banjaxed, eleven stone one morning and something else the next, so maybe i'm up with the fluid, maybe i'm not. i genuinely don't know.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): what tablets?

[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): the amlodopine, five milligrams... no, amlodipine, ten milligrams, they put it up, one in the morning. and the water tablet, bendroflumethiazide, two point five milligrams, once a day. my brother has the diabetes, he's on metformin, a gram twice a day he tells me, but that's him, not me.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): home blood pressure?

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): i've a machine off the chemist. yesterday morning it was one thirty two over eighty four, and sunday evening one twenty eight over seventy eight. at home it's always lower. in here i get nervy, i can feel it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): medicine allergies?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): no, nothing. penicillin for a tooth years ago and i was grand.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): right. ankles.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): pitting oedema, both ankles, left worse. chest clear, no crackles. heart sounds normal, no murmur.

[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): i was worried it was the heart, because an uncle dropped dead years back, but he was a smoker and i'm not, i never smoked, not even when everyone did. and he married in, he's not blood, so maybe that doesn't count at all.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): the swelling is most likely the amlodipine. the frequent passing of urine fits the water tablet. i'm not calling this heart failure.

[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): so do i stop it? the chemist said the same, your man behind the counter, but i didn't want to quit it myself with the pressure up in the clinic and grand at home. it didn't sit right with me to just stop.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): stop the amlodipine today. start losartan fifty milligrams once a day instead. keep the bendroflumethiazide.

[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): err losartan, fifty, once a day, grand. and the water tablet still with the breakfast, after the porridge, that's how i remember it. will the ankles actually go down or am i stuck like this?
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): keep it with breakfast. ankles should ease over a couple of weeks. put the legs up in the evening.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): kidney bloods before you start the losartan. the nurse will book you this afternoon.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): i can put him on the half two list. there's a slot.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): half two is grand, i'll wait, i've the paper. will i bring the home readings next time? i've a notebook, the writing is desperate but i can copy it out fair.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): yes, bring the notebook. i'll see you in four weeks.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): four weeks, right so. and if they swell worse before that, or i go dizzy on the new one, what then? i get wound up about new tablets, i read the leaflet back to front.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): if the swelling gets worse or you feel faint, come back sooner. don't wait the four weeks.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): grand, i hear you. and i won't be taking my sister's biotin either, she offered it for the nails, swears by it, but that's hers from boots, i said no.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): good. amlodipine stopped, losartan after the bloods tonight, back in four weeks.

spec.situation: Patient on amlodipine and a water tablet with swollen ankles and passing urine often; blood pressure read at clinic and at home with different numbers; doctor changes one medicine.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Amlodipine 10 mg morning is supported; discontinued was instructed by doctor, not reported by patient.
bad.text: amlodipine (dose=10 mg, frequency=once daily in the morning, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Current bendroflumethiazide 2.5 mg daily supported; 'with breakfast' is later instruction, not original frequency.
bad.text: bendroflumethiazide (dose=2.5 mg, frequency=once daily with breakfast, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

Home blood pressure readings were reported as 132/84 yesterday morning and 128/78 Sunday evening, with patient stating home readings are usually lower.

Kidney blood test was booked for this afternoon at half two.

Doctor asked about weight change and patient said he genuinely did not know because the scales were unreliable; possible fluid-related weight change was uncertain.
The patient stated he had previously tolerated penicillin without reaction ('penicillin for a tooth years ago and I was grand'), supporting the no-known-drug-allergy history.
